instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The caterer still has your wedding date. Sit down before you call the venue, please; I have the changes in order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has someone else got our room?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No one has the room. The building can't be used, but don't cancel the caterer; that's a separate booking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we move into their smaller hall?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The fire reached that hall too. Start with the outdoor reception plan, please. I'll read the available spaces one at a time; you don't have to choose while I'm still explaining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your garden gnome is home. Leave the box flat, please; I'll unpack it with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is there so much padding? I can lift him out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lift the packets separately. He isn't in one piece, but each piece is wrapped so we can put him together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All the pieces? I want his fishing rod back on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The rod hasn't come back. Start with the face, please; we have the whole smile. I'll lay out what we've got before we discuss replacing anything.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Confess Around Them
cards.instruction: Use partial admissions to make a reciprocal confession feel like the only missing piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I changed the meeting time to three. Let's reconstruct it accurately: what happened to the room booking?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You changed the time without telling me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I didn't send you the amended invitation. Put my time change and missed notice in the first column; the room column is still blank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I moved us upstairs because builders had the old room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then enter who received that message. My unsent invitation says three in the old room; please show me where your room notice went so we can finish the two columns.

beats.text: I kept the first complaint letter in my drawer. Put that down before we discuss the second one.

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: It Was Foreshadowed
cards.instruction: Turn the failure into a planned turning point by returning to earlier details that now appear to predict it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the first wobble in our baking video. The cake collapsing is the planned turning point; don't cut its setup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ignored me when I said it was leaning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That warning needs to stay too. Please put it before the close-up; viewers must see why the collapse matters.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no cake left to film for the ending.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Film the empty stand for five seconds. Use your earlier warning as the last sound, then cut to black.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tent fell exactly where our story turns. I mentioned that loose peg and told you to keep your waterproof coat nearby.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were supposed to fix the peg, not make a story out of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'd lose the warning. Please note the peg before we rebuild; the recovery only makes sense if we keep the cause.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can the recovery start now? I'm getting soaked.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put on the coat I told you to keep ready. Fasten it before helping with the pole, please; that earlier instruction is what gets us through this part.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Be Right in Retrospect
cards.instruction: Perform certainty by reinterpreting every surprise as something your earlier words were obviously predicting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I said we'd 'open up and let things flow'. So far, accurate. Close the kitchen stopcock first, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You meant dinner conversation, not a burst pipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please read the whole phrase before correcting the forecast. The flow was explicit; we've reached that part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The plumber says he'll have to open the ceiling to reach the leak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's 'open up'. Ask him for the exact section before he cuts, please. I'd like the work kept to the scope I predicted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I forecast a sunny holiday, I meant the refund brightening your week. Please distinguish weather from outcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain ruined every day. You told me to pack sunscreen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you brought it home unused. Keep it sealed, please; that return can brighten the outcome further.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shop won't refund it. It came free with the suitcase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then record it as a retained benefit, not a lost expense. You still have sunscreen for the next trip; please don't close a forecast before all its benefits arrive.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Reverse the Score
cards.instruction: Turn each apparent loss into a new category of victory, then invite comparison on those changing terms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last in the race, first in route appreciation. Let's compare what we noticed; start with plants, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a speed contest. I got to the finish first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's one category. Count the plants you identified, not how fast you passed them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I named ten. You called every flower a daisy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I win for consistency. One label throughout; please use the same measure for both of us. How many times did you have to change yours?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My small trophy wins on storage. Put yours beside it and measure the space each needs, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is the consolation prize. Mine is first place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's rank, not storage. Keep the handles inside your measurement; they don't become invisible because you won.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The handles frame the word 'FIRST'. That's what people will look at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then compare restraint. Mine only has the date; yours needs its result in capitals. Read both inscriptions aloud and tell me which asks for less attention.
